senses.gloss: m. (פטט, cmp. פתת) [something minute, tender,] one of the clay pins forming a sort of tripod for the support of a pot, peg.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 8:4">Sabb. VIII, 4</cite> <he>כדי לעשות פ׳</he> a quantity of clay large enough for a peg.—[<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 785:40">Yalk. Num. 785</cite> <he>פּוּט של מנורה</he> the peg for a candlestick v., however, quot. fr. Sifré Zuṭṭa in R. S. to <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 11:2">Kel. XI, 2</cite>.]—Pl. <he>פִּטְפּוּטִים</he>, <cite ref="Q00545"><he>פִּטְפּוּטִין</he></cite>, <cite ref="Q00061"><he>פִּי׳</he></cite>, (<cite ref="Q00545"><he>פִּטְפְּטִין</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Shabbat 102b:6">Sabb. 102ᵇ</cite> <he>עני עושה פִּיטְפּוּטֵי כירה קטנה וכ׳</he> a poor man makes pegs for a small stove to put on it a small pot (which is also called building).

<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 5:11">Kel. V, 11</cite> <he>עשה לה פ׳</he> if he made legs for the stove (so that it no longer rests immediately on the ground); <cite ref="Tosefta Kelim Kamma 4:20">Tosef. Kel. B. Kam. IV, 20</cite>.

<cite ref="Tosefta Kelim Kamma 5:1">Ib. V, 1</cite> <he>שלשה … פטפט׳ שנתנן וכ׳</he> three pegs, three pins or three legs stuck in the ground and joined with clay to put a pot on them; <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 6:1">Kel. VI, 1</cite>. Tosef. l. c. 7 <he>פטפוטי</he> (read <he>טין …</he>). Ib. 8. Ib. 9 <he>ארבעה פטפוטי כירה וכ׳</he> four legs of a stove &c.; a. e.
